Price tables are the least useful part of the decision, because the thing that actually breaks when you switch providers is never the price — it is the model id, the streaming shape, or a minimum top-up you did not notice. I run the API side of a small reseller, so read the honest parts below as self-interest in both directions: I want you to test your endpoint properly, and I also want to tell you when switching is a bad idea. articles.body: You’ve just integrated an AI agent into your FinTech platform to handle customer queries or automate credit risk analysis. It’s running smoothly, until you realize you might be letting it see sensitive info it shouldn’t , or worse, you have no solid audit trail to prove compliance with data regulations. Getting the AI working was the easy part; locking down data privacy and compliance without breaking the AI’s usefulness? That’s the headache. The FinTech AI Privacy Puzzle In FinTech, data is gold and liability. Regulations like GDPR, CCPA, PCI-DSS, and others impose strict rules on what data can be accessed, how it’s logged, and how long it’s retained.

articles.body: Radical Minimalism: A Guide to the Pi Coding Agent Workflow The Pi coding agent workflow is a minimalist approach to AI-assisted software engineering that prioritizes transparency, low token costs, and developer control. By using a terminal-based interface with only four core tools—read, write, edit, and bash—it allows senior engineers to orchestrate complex refactoring and feature development without the bloat of traditional AI IDEs. What This Workflow Does Pi is not your typical AI chatbot. Created by Mario Zechner, it is designed as a 'harness' for large language models. The core philosophy is that the AI should be a tool in the developer's terminal, not a black box that hides its reasoning.

articles.body: Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. articles.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
articles.excerpt: Colorful metaphors, a near-miss with Eddie Murphy and humpback whales in 20th-century California.
articles.body: It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters.
